english: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers with $a>0$ and $a+b>0$. Let $F:\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\to\mathbb{R}$ and $G:(-\pi,\pi)\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable functions such that $F(0)=G(0)=0$,

for all $x$ in their respective domains. If $F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=G\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=G\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$, then the value of $a^{2}+b^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$ तथा $b$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं जिनके लिए $a>0$ तथा $a+b>0$ है। माना कि $F:\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\to\mathbb{R}$ तथा $G:(-\pi,\pi)\to\mathbb{R}$ अवकलनीय फलन हैं जिनके लिए $F(0)=G(0)=0$ है, तथा अपने-अपने प्रांत के सभी $x$ के लिए
हैं। यदि $F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=G\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ तथा $F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=G\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ है, तो $a^{2}+b^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Dividing, $\dfrac{\tan^{-1}(\sqrt3s)}{\tan^{-1}s}$ is strictly decreasing in $s>0$ and equals the right side at $s=\dfrac12$; so $s=\dfrac12$ and then $as=2$
solution_full: For $G$ on $(-\pi,\pi)$ put $t=\tan\dfrac x2$: $\cos x=\dfrac{1-t^{2}}{1+t^{2}}$ and $dx=\dfrac{2\,dt}{1+t^{2}}$, so $\dfrac{dx}{5+3\cos x}=\dfrac{2\,dt}{5(1+t^{2})+3(1-t^{2})}=\dfrac{2\,dt}{8+2t^{2}}=\dfrac{dt}{4+t^{2}}$.
For $F$ on $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ divide numerator and denominator by $\cos^{2}x$: $\dfrac{\sec^{2}x\,dx}{a\sec^{2}x+b\tan^{2}x}=\dfrac{du}{a+(a+b)u^{2}}$ with $u=\tan x$.
With $s=\sqrt{\dfrac{a+b}{a}}>0$: $F(x)=\dfrac{1}{a s}\tan^{-1}(s\tan x)$, so $F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{\tan^{-1}s}{as}$ and $F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{\tan^{-1}(\sqrt3 s)}{as}$.
The left side decreases strictly from $\sqrt3$ (as $s\to0^{+}$) towards $\dfrac23$ (as $s\to\infty$), so the equation has exactly one root, and $s=\dfrac12$ is that root.
Check: $4-3\sin^{2}x=\dfrac{5+3\cos2x}{2}$, so $F(x)=G(2x)$ for all $x$, consistent with both conditions.
originality_note: New: an unknown integrand of the a + b sin^2 x type is identified from two values of its antiderivative, which are matched with values of the tan(x/2)-antiderivative of 1/(5 + 3 cos x); the hidden fact is F(x) = G(2x) (way 4). Closest known: separate textbook integrals of 1/(a + b sin^2 x) and 1/(a + b cos x). Different because: the two methods must be compared through their antiderivatives and the parameters recovered from two equations.
key_step: Integrating both forms (tan x and tan(x/2) substitutions) and matching tan^-1(s)/(as) with (1/2) tan^-1(1/2) to get s = 1/2, a = 4.
justification: Two standard integrals and a matching of parameters; the matching is guided by the structure. A routine multi-step chain without a real insight, level 2 like 2026-P2-Q12 (L2), which also recovers unknowns from two given values.
